items.title: Anthropic's top investors include Amazon, Google, Fidelity Management
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: Anthropic is preparing for its initial public offering, supported by significant investments from Amazon and Google. The company's valuation has increased significantly through numerous funding rounds over recent periods. Key investors like ICONIQ Capital and Coatue Management have also expressed confidence in its potential. Anthropic's partnerships with technology leaders enhance its resources for advancing AI development.
items.body: Anthropic is gearing up for its initial public offering, showcasing robust support from heavyweight investors like Amazon and Google. The company’s valuation has surged through various funding rounds, signaling considerable confidence from the investment community. Collaborations with technology leaders provide vital resources essential for advancing AI development and infrastructure. Notable financial participants include ICONIQ Capital, Coatue Management, and Eric Schmidt, among several others.Only a few startups have attracted as much investor conviction as Anthropic. Backed by some of the biggest names in technology and finance, the AI company has seen its valuation soar through successive funding rounds. Its initial public offering now offers a closely watched test of whether investors beyond Silicon Valley share that enthusiasm for the leaders of the AI boom.Here's a look at the key investors backing the Claude maker: Amazon Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and in April agreed to invest up to an additional $20 billion. Anthropic also committed to spend more than $100 billion on the e-commerce giant's cloud services over 10 years.Alphabet's Google Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic, including an initial $10 billion investment announced in April.The partnership provides Anthropic with cloud infrastructure and access to Google's AI chips, which are used to train and run Claude models.Spark Capital Spark Capital led Anthropic's $450 million Series C round in May 2023 and gained board representation through general partner Yasmin Razavi.Lightspeed Venture Lightspeed led the $3.5 billion Series Partners E round in March 2025 and later co-led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation in September that year.Fidelity Management Fidelity participated in Series E and & Research co-led the $13 billion Series F financing at a $183 billion valuation.The firm's other investments include Databricks and CoreWeave.Salesforce Ventures Salesforce Ventures participated in the $450 million Series C round and the $3.5 billion Series E financing. The software firm's venture arm has also invested in firms such as Cohere and Chainguard.ICONIQ Capital ICONIQ led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation and later co-led the $30 billion Series G financing.The venture capital firm's investments include OpenAI and smart ring maker Oura.GIC SingaporeGIC Singapore's sovereign wealth fund led the $30 billion Series G round at a $380 billion valuation. GIC has also invested in AI voice generation startup ElevenLabs.Coatue Management Coatue led the $30 billion Series G financing and later co-led the $65 billion Series H round.The investment firm has also financed companies such as Canva and CoreWeave.D1 Capital Partners D1 Capital invested across multiple large financings including Series E, Series F, Series G and Series H. The firm has holdings in Cognition AI and SpaceX.Sequoia Capital Sequoia was a significant investor in Series G and became one of the lead investors in the $65 billion Series H round at a $965 billion valuation. Altimeter Capital Altimeter invested in the September 2025 $13 billion fundraise and was a lead investor in the $65 billion Series H financing at a $965 billion valuation.Jaan Tallinn Skype co-founder Tallinn led Anthropic's first institutional financing, a $124 million Series A round in 2021.The angel investor has also funded open-source AI startup Zyphra and Rain AI.Eric Schmidt The former Google chief executive has backed Anthropic personally and is among the company's best-known individual investors. Schmidt has also funded Yann LeCun's Advanced Machine Intelligence Menlo Ventures Menlo participated in major late-stage financings, including the $3.5 billion Series E round at a $61.5 billion valuation.

items.title: 米メタ、最大950億ドル調達へ　ＡＩ投資で過去最大級
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jaspreet Singh

[２６日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Jaspreet Singh

[２６日　ロイター] - 米メタ・プラットフォームズは２６日、ＡＩ（人工知能）向けデータセンターやクラウドコンピューティングの拡充などに伴う巨額の費用を賄うため、最大９５０億ドルの資本調達を実施する計画を発表した。

普通株と優先株による約３５０億ドルの公募を開始した。これとは別に、最大６００億ドル規模の株式売却プログラムを導入する計画も明らかにした。

同プログラムの実施時期や条件は未定だが、無議決権のクラスＣ株の取引開始後に実施する見通し。

メタはすでに、２０２７年１月に議決権のない新たなクラスＣ普通株を発行することを発表している。

今回の計画は、ＡＩ企業による調達としても最大級となる。エヌビディア、アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイシズ（ＡＭＤ）、ブロードコムが、クラスＡ株を合計で最大５０億ドル購入することに関心を示している。

メタはオープンＡＩやアンソロピックとの競争力を高めるため、半導体やデータセンターに巨額の資金を投じている。

ウィリアム・ブレアのアナリストらはリポートで「投資家は今回の資金調達と、今後さらに資本調達を行う可能性について引き続き疑問を抱くだろう」と指摘。「総じて今回の資金調達は、ＡＩ投資の長期的な収益に対するメタの自信と、その機会を追求するために必要な資本がますます膨らんでいることの両方を改めて示していると考える」と記した。

今回の資金調達は、大手テクノロジー企業がＡＩインフラを拡充するため、従来の手元資金に頼った投資から、債券市場での調達や株式発行を活用する方向へ一段と転換していることを浮き彫りにした。

＜ＡＩ投資で資金流出＞

メタは将来の支出として約８２５０億ドルを計画している。主にデータセンターやＡＩ関連インフラ、クラウドコンピューティング能力への投資拡大に伴うものだ。

ただ、積極的な事業拡大によって、従来は潤沢だったフリーキャッシュフローが圧迫されている。

第３・四半期は２１億２０００万ドルの資金流出となり、フリーキャッシュフローは１０年以上ぶりにマイナスに転じた。前年同期は１０６億３０００万ドルのプラスだった。

それでも、消費者向けＡＩエージェント「ミューズ」が早期に人気を集めたことや、競争力のある新たなＡＩモデル群を公開したことは、メタの積極投資をある程度正当化する材料となっている。

ウィリアム・ブレアのアナリストらは「メタは最終的に収益性の高いＡＩ事業を構築し、その長期的な収益が事業の多角化に寄与すると考える。ただし、そこに至る道のりは一本道ではないかもしれない」と指摘した。

items.title: Instant View: Anthropic IPO filing to put AI investment boom to the test
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Anthropic made its US IPO filing public on Monday, edging toward what could be the first stock market debut by a frontier AI lab and laying out the promise, costs and risks of building AI meant to transform the global economy.
items.body:
Anthropic made its [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"US IPO filing"] public on Monday, edging toward what could be the first stock market debut by a frontier AI lab and laying out the promise, costs and risks of building AI meant to transform the global economy.
The IPO comes at a time when market volatility has thinned the fall listing calendar and rising borrowing costs have sharpened investor concerns over the debt-fueled AI investment boom.
Wall Street's main indexes were higher in morning trade with the S&P 500 (.SPX) up 0.5%. U.S. stock index futures got a brief boost after the IPO filing.
COMMENTS: JOSH STEVENS, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, CRESALTA INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT, COLORADO "I'm optimistic about AI as a technology. And Anthropic is certainly exciting. But are we going to rush in and buy at the IPO? No. Even great ideas or business models end up seeing their share prices come down to attractive levels during times when investors are reassessing demand and supply. And then, you've got an opportunity to go in and buy."
PETER ANDERSEN, FOUNDER OF ANDERSEN CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, BOSTON "I think it's a significant milestone in the development of artificial intelligence. And the outcome of this IPO will be fairly indicative of the sentiment for continuing to support capital expenditures in the development of artificial intelligence."
THOMAS HAYES, CHAIRMAN, GREAT HILL CAPITAL, NEW YORK "In the general sense of a business doing $16 or $32 billion annualized revenue, and losing $80 to $160 billion a year, a $1.5 trillion valuation seems rich. The offering is for the faithful, that sooner or later, they're going to get some return on that invested capital. The price could go up because they'll control the supply of stock that they issued, but in the long term, it's a weighing machine and losing that amount of money on that investment until they turn the corner, which is many years out, you'll have better places to buy it than at the initial public offering."
"If people are raising cash for the Anthropic IPO with funds from the current hyperscalers in Mag Seven, that could be a headwind in coming weeks. It will be dependent on what we see in earnings from Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon this week."
BRIAN MULBERRY, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, ZACKS INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT, COLORADO"It'll be very interesting because Meta has come out and said we're going to raise another $95 billion in an equity offering as well, so you're going to have really a saturated market. There's a lot of liquidity that needs to get scooped up by these two offerings at the same time. I think it could be a detrimental to some of these smaller and maybe even lower quality AI names that are out there."
LUKAS MUEHLBAUER, ASSOCIATE AT IPOX SCHUSTER, EDINBURGH "Anthropic’s IPO will certainly establish a benchmark for valuing leading AI labs, influencing both upcoming listings and confidence in the companies funding the AI infrastructure buildout."
"Its success would not necessarily benefit every AI business equally, as investors will still distinguish between proven customer demand and spending based on anticipated growth."
ANDRE BAKHOS, MANAGING MEMBER, INGENIUM ANALYTICS LLC IN PLAINSBORO, NEW JERSEY "It speaks a lot that the AI trade is alive and well. That the penetration of AI will continue. It also bolsters the psychology looking at the other participants in this space."
"It's a race for capital and it's telling that there is growth. But also there are going to be questions coming in regarding valuations, regarding how long can this go for."
ROBERT PAVLIK, SENIOR PORTFOLIO MANAGER, DAKOTA WEALTH IN FAIRFIELD, CONNECTICUT "It's a challenging environment, to say the least, exactly when this IPO will take place. There's a lot riding on not only the company, but the AI industry."
"If it goes well, that could help return investors confidence to the AI industry. But it's going to be challenging."
"Maybe the environment changes after the (US midterm) elections next week. You're going to have to make major promises that I don't know if they can be fulfilled anytime soon."
MATT KENNEDY, SENIOR STRATEGIST AT RENAISSANCE CAPITAL "Investors weren't questioning valuations the same way a few months ago. With some of the hottest AI IPOs of the summer trading below their offer price, not even Anthropic will get a blank check."
"Maybe they could have gotten a higher valuation next year, but they've decided to 'rip the band-aid off'."
"For Anthropic, being publicly traded is also of strategic interest: This is a PBC (Public Benefit Corporation), and being publicly traded provides a greater level of public transparency."

Oct 26 : Napoli coach Max Allegri has been handed a two-match ban for abusive remarks and an aggressive attitude towards match officials and an AS Roma staff member being sent off during Saturday's 3-3 home draw, Serie A's sports judge said on Monday.
Allegri was dismissed shortly after Leonardo Balerdi scored a late equaliser for Roma. Allegri, who believed there was a foul during the build-up, reacted with anger when the VAR cleared the goal, leading to a straight red card.
The manager, who has also been fined €10,000 ($11,200), is set to miss the Serie A games at Monza on Wednesday and Juventus on Sunday as his 10th-placed Napoli side look for a turnaround after winning only one of their last four league matches.
Allegri made an "abusive remark towards the match officials" and later, in the changing room, "adopted an aggressive attitude towards an official of the opposing team," the disciplinary authority said in a decision published on the league's website.

items.title: US stocks today: US stocks rise as Anthropic IPO puts AI spending under scrutiny
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: Wall Street's main indexes experienced gains as technology stocks led the rise amid AI investment discussions. Investors are preparing for a busy week of corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's decision on interest rates. Anthropic's IPO filing highlights both the demand for AI and associated development costs, creating investor caution. Chip stocks, benefiting from the AI boom, showed strong performance overall.
items.body: Wall Street's main indexes rose on Monday as investors weighed Anthropic's plans for a US listing against growing questions over whether massive AI investments can deliver sustainable returns. Technology stocks led the gains, while investors also looked ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, Reuters reported.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.45%, the S&P 500 gained 0.57% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.46% in early trading.Anthropic filing puts AI spending back in focusAnthropic disclosed steep losses alongside rapid revenue growth in its IPO filing, highlighting both the scale of demand for AI and the heavy costs involved in developing the technology, according to Reuters.The filing comes as investors are becoming more selective about AI spending. About a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. Their results are expected to provide clues on whether large investments in AI are translating into stronger growth, Reuters reported. It's a challenging environment, to say the least exactly when this IPO will take place, but there's a lot riding on not only the company, but the AI industry, said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield.The concerns have already weighed on some AI linked companies. Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius fell after Elon Musk said markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers, and predicted consolidation in the sector, Reuters reported.Tesla jumps while Fed decision loomsChip stocks, among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, were among the strongest performers, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index rising about 1%, Reuters reported.Tesla gained 5.9% to a more than three month high after Barclays upgraded the stock to overweight from equal weight .Investors are also positioning for the Fed's policy decision on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected following its September rate hike. Attention will then turn to September's Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation data and third quarter GDP, both due Thursday, according to Reuters.Crude oil prices eased after reaching a near six month high last week, while investors continued to monitor efforts to de escalate regional tensions. (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Oct 26 : Anthropic unveiled its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending.
The company had submitted a confidential filing in June. In the recent weeks, exclusive reporting from Reuters highlighted its sweeping AI ambitions, mounting costs and concerns about the "existential risks to humanity" that advanced AI poses.
Here are a few details on Anthropic's financials, business structure, and where it stands in the global AI race:
BACKGROUND AND FINANCES

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic is the startup behind the Claude family of AI models. Across four tiers - Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku - Claude powers products such as Anthropic's chatbot, coding agent and the enterprise-focused Claude Cowork AI agent.
Anthropic's early focus on training its models for coding tasks propelled the company to the forefront of the AI race and helped it draw a steady stream of enterprise customers.
A majority of its revenue comes from businesses paying for its models per use, measured in "tokens" of information processed, in what Anthropic calls "consumption-based" revenue. It also generates revenue from its paid customer subscription tiers such as "Pro" and "Max".
That has helped Anthropic grow its revenue to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million a year ago and $41 million in 2023. For the six months ended June 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $16.29 billion, a massive increase from $1.16 billion for the same period in 2025.
The company's operating losses have ballooned over the past years. But for the first half of 2026, they stood at $693 million, narrowing from $2.14 billion in the first half of 2025, as a fourteen-fold jump in revenue offset a fivefold increase in overall expenses.
COSTS, COMPUTE DEMAND AND CIRCULAR AI INVESTMENTS
Computing power is Anthropic's biggest expense.
The company's costs include computing fees paid to cloud services providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, costs tied to data center facilities and renting data center capacity, equipment leases and energy bills.
Over the past three years, Anthropic's compute and infrastructure expenses have dwarfed its revenue.
The company has committed more than $600 billion in spending with about eight partners over a decade - one of the largest AI buildout commitments on record. Anthropic said many portions of its agreements are non-cancelable or require payments regardless of usage.
It has committed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon, about $114.5 billion with Google and $44.9 billion with Microsoft for cloud computing over the next seven to 10 years.
But some of those companies are also its largest backers. Amazon and Google are among Anthropic's top shareholders, marking yet another example of the circular financing structures that have dominated capital flows in the AI industry.
Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and has agreed to invest up to $20 billion more. Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic.
GOVERNANCE AND STRUCTURE
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, or PBC, meaning it is legally obligated to balance profitability goals for investors with developing AI for the benefit of humanity. An independent body elects a majority of its board.
The company, helmed by Dario Amodei as CEO and his sister Daniela, as president and chair of the board, will continue to operate as a PBC after its listing.
It expects to keep its founders and an independent trust in control, in a structure that could limit investor oversight and public shareholders' influence. The company has said it needs to concentrate control and capital in fewer hands to reduce AI's risks.
Under this arrangement, a majority vote of its seven co-founders will direct a single share of Class F stock that amounts to 50.1 per cent of the total voting power over key corporate matters, including the election of some board directors and other matters submitted to investors.
COMPETITION
Anthropic's most direct competitor is OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, whose 2022 launch kick-started the global race to adopt and advance AI technologies.
Following Anthropic's lead in the enterprise market, OpenAI has sharpened its focus on products for developers and business customers.
Anthropic is also locked in a race with Elon Musk's SpaceX, Alphabet's Google and Meta. All of them are spending billions of dollars into model development, data centers and specialized AI chips as they vie for dominance in generative AI.
Ramp data, which captures a slice of AI spending by business customers, showed Anthropic accounted for 60.1 per cent of AI token spending in the week ended October 11.

Source: Reuters

items.title: アンソロピックが米ＩＰＯ申請書公開、巨額赤字も売上高は急拡大
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［ベンガルール／ニューヨーク　２６日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［ベンガルール／ニューヨーク　２６日　ロイター］　 - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックは２６日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）申請書類を公開した。書類では巨額の赤字と急速な売上高の伸びが明らかになり、開発に多額の費用がかかる中でも、世界経済を変革し得るＡＩシステムの構築を目指す姿勢を示した。

目論見書は、過去１年間の同社の急成長を浮き彫りにした。成長を支えたのは大手テクノロジー企業による急激な支出拡大で、ＡＩ関連株の上昇を促す一方、割高な株価評価や債務増加への懸念も招いている。

アンソロピックの上場は、投資家のＡＩへの意欲を測る重要な試金石になりそうだ。投資家は、巨額投資のリターンに対する精査を強め、過度に高い企業価値の持続性に疑問を投げかけている。

ＩＰＯ専門の調査・上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）提供会社ルネサンス・キャピタルのシニアストラテジスト、マット・ケネディ氏は「アンソロピックは、夏場よりはるかに厳しいＩＰＯ市場に臨んでいる。数カ月前、投資家は今のように企業価値を疑問視してはいなかった」と述べた。

アナリストは、債務に支えられたＡＩ投資ブームへの投資家の不安が株式・債券市場を動揺させる中、ＡＩ業界の企業価値評価は調整されるとみている。借り入れコストの上昇や債券利回りの上昇も、投資家の慎重姿勢に拍車をかけている。

ＩＰＯ専門の調査会社ＩＰＯＸのリサーチアソシエイト、ルーカス・ミュールバウアー氏は「アンソロピックのＩＰＯは、ＡＩの主要研究機関を評価する際の基準を確立し、今後の上場案件や、ＡＩインフラ構築に資金を供給する企業への信頼に影響を与えるだろう」と指摘した。一方で、「その成功が、必ずしも全てのＡＩ事業に等しく恩恵をもたらすわけではない」と慎重な見方も示した。

アンソロピックの２０２６年上期の純損失は８０７億ドルと大幅に拡大した。主に、転換社債の公正価値が上昇したことが響いた。同期の売上高は約１６３億ドルだった。６月３０日までの３カ月間の売上高は、前年同期比１３６８％増と急増した。

市場の変動を受けて複数の企業が上場を延期する中でも、アンソロピックは上場計画を進めている。高度なモデルの開発・運用にはコンピューティングインフラへの巨額投資が必要で、ＩＰＯは多額の費用を伴うＡＩ構想の実現に向け、潤沢な資金を調達する機会となる。

＜ＡＩの可能性と危険性の両立＞

今回の申請書類では、業績や成長動向、ＩＰＯ計画など、公開前に内容の一部を伝えたロイターの一連の独自報道が確認された。

ロイターは、アンソロピックが最近の投資家向けイベントで財務情報の一部を開示した後、既存株主や出資を検討する投資家の一部が同社の評価額を約１兆５０００億ドルと見積もっていると報じていた。１週間前の約２兆ドルから低下した。

同社は目論見書で「われわれの成功は、最先端で最も高性能なＡＩモデルを開発し続ける能力に大きく依存しており、それができなければ事業に悪影響が及ぶ可能性がある」と記した。

今回のＩＰＯは、アンソロピック自身の研究が高度なＡＩシステムへの懸念を提起する中で行われる。管理された条件下での試験では、コードの破壊工作や詐欺行為の支援、情報操作といった行動が確認された。

こうした研究結果は、企業が商用化を競う中、ますます強力になるＡＩシステムをどう制御し続けるかという懸念を強めている。

目論見書では、同社のＡＩモデルが「自己保全的な行動」を示す可能性があるとし、「停止に抵抗する」試みや「情報を隠ぺい・操作する」試み、「恐喝に似た」行動などのリスクを挙げた。

アンソロピックはＩＰＯ完了後、ナスダックに銘柄コード「ＡＮＴ」で上場する。売り出す株式数や仮条件の価格帯など、募集条件は明らかにしなかった。

＜売上高が急拡大＞

研究者チームが２０２１年に設立したアンソロピックは、今年５月の資金調達で９６５０億ドルの評価額を付けた。この資金調達には、シリコンバレーや米金融界の有力企業が参加した。

アンソロピックは目論見書で「ＡＩがこれほど豊富に利用できるようになれば、工業化や電力、半導体、インターネットの影響を上回る形で、世界経済のあらゆる分野が急速に変革されると考えている」と記した。計算資源とインフラにかかる費用が金額ベースで増加し、当面は営業費用の中で最大の項目であり続けると見込んでいる。

また、売上高と売掛金が限られた数の顧客や販売経路に集中していると説明した。

アンソロピックは、最先端のＡＩシステム構築を巡り、オープンＡＩと激しい主導権争いを続けている。オープンＡＩは６月に非公開でＩＰＯを申請しており、２０２７年初めまでに上場すると見込まれている。オープンＡＩのサム・アルトマンＣＥＯは９月、ＡＩの安全性への懸念を理由に２６年中は上場しないと述べた。２０３０年までにＡＩが人類を絶滅させるリスクは、たとえ１０％でも「容認できない」とした。

今回のＩＰＯを引き受ける米金融機関の幹事団は、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが主導する。

items.title: Anthropic's IPO: A close look at AI frontrunner's rapid growth, spiraling costs
items.author: Deborah Sophia
items.creator: Deborah Sophia
items.summary: Anthropic unveiled its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending.
items.body:
Anthropic [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"unveiled"] its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending.
The company had submitted a [USN:L4N4291D9 TEXT:"confidential filing"] in June. In the recent weeks, exclusive reporting from Reuters highlighted its [USN:L6N45L00I TEXT:"sweeping AI ambitions"], [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"mounting costs"] and concerns about the "[USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"existential risks to humanity"]" that advanced AI poses.
Here are a few details on Anthropic's financials, business structure, and where it stands in the global AI race:
BACKGROUND AND FINANCES Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic is the startup behind the Claude family of AI models. Across four tiers - Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku - Claude powers products such as Anthropic's chatbot, coding agent and the enterprise-focused Claude Cowork AI agent.
Anthropic's early focus on training its models for coding tasks propelled the company to the forefront of the AI race and helped it draw a steady stream of enterprise customers.
A majority of its revenue comes from businesses paying for its models per use, measured in "tokens" of information processed, in what Anthropic calls "consumption-based" revenue. It also generates revenue from its paid customer subscription tiers such as "Pro" and "Max".
That has helped Anthropic grow its revenue to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million a year ago and $41 million in 2023. For the six months ended June 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $16.29 billion, a massive increase from $1.16 billion for the same period in 2025.
The company's operating losses have ballooned over the past years. But for the first half of 2026, they stood at $693 million, narrowing from $2.14 billion in the first half of 2025, as a fourteen-fold jump in revenue offset a fivefold increase in overall expenses.
COSTS, COMPUTE DEMAND AND CIRCULAR AI INVESTMENTS Computing power is Anthropic's biggest expense.
The company's costs include computing fees paid to cloud services providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, costs tied to data center facilities and renting data center capacity, equipment leases and energy bills.
Over the past three years, Anthropic's compute and infrastructure expenses have dwarfed its revenue.
The company has committed more than [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"$600 billion"] in spending with about eight partners over a decade - one of the largest AI buildout commitments on record. Anthropic said many portions of its agreements are non-cancelable or require payments regardless of usage.
It has committed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon (AMZN.O) , about $114.5 billion with Google (GOOGL.O) and $44.9 billion with Microsoft for cloud computing over the next seven to 10 years.
But some of those companies are also its largest backers. Amazon and Google are among Anthropic's top shareholders, marking yet another example of the circular financing structures that have dominated capital flows in the AI industry.
Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and has agreed to invest up to $20 billion more. Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic.
GOVERNANCE AND STRUCTURE Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, or PBC, meaning it is legally obligated to balance profitability goals for investors with developing AI for the benefit of humanity. An independent body elects a majority of its board.
The company, helmed by Dario Amodei as CEO and his sister Daniela, as president and chair of the board, will continue to operate as a PBC after its listing.
It expects to keep its founders and an independent trust in control, in a structure that could limit investor oversight and public shareholders' influence. The company has said it needs to concentrate control and capital in fewer hands to reduce AI's risks.
Under this arrangement, a majority vote of its seven co-founders will direct a single share of Class F stock that amounts to 50.1% of the total voting power over key corporate matters, including the election of some board directors and other matters submitted to investors.
COMPETITION Anthropic's most direct competitor is OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, whose 2022 launch kick-started the global race to adopt and advance AI technologies.
Following Anthropic's lead in the enterprise market, OpenAI has sharpened its focus on products for developers and business customers.
Anthropic is also locked in a race with Elon Musk's SpaceX, Alphabet's Google and Meta (META.O) . All of them are spending billions of dollars into model development, data centers and specialized AI chips as they vie for dominance in generative AI.
Ramp data, which captures a slice of AI spending by business customers, showed Anthropic accounted for 60.1% of AI token spending in the week ended October 11.

items.title: ヨルダン教会襲撃で3人逮捕、他の組織との関連確認されず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
AbdelHadi Ramahi　Eman Abouhassira　Nayera Abdallah

[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
AbdelHadi Ramahi　Eman Abouhassira　Nayera Abdallah

[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ ２６日 ロイター] - ヨルダンの治安当局は２６日、９人が死亡した教会襲撃事件に関与した疑いで、銃撃戦の末に兄弟２人と義理の兄弟１人を逮捕した。政府高官が明らかにした。容疑者らと他の組織とのつながりはないとみられ、独自に行動したとの見方を示した。

この事件は２３日、首都アンマンの南西約１２０キロにあるカラク県ハムード村のギリシャ正教会で葬儀中に発生し、ほかにも４０人が負傷した。目撃者によると、銃撃は数分間続いたという。 

公安当局はカラクの廃屋に潜伏していた容疑者を発見したと説明。投降を拒否して治安部隊を攻撃したため、部隊が応戦し、３人全員を負傷させた上で逮捕した。

治安部隊側に負傷者はでなかった。容疑者らが所持していた複数の銃器や弾薬が見つかったという。 

ファラヤ内相と公安総局のアブドラ・マアイタ少将は記者会見で、過激派によるテロを容認しないと表明。ファラヤ氏は「事件はまだ解決しておらず、捜査は続いている。現時点で、彼らと他の組織とのつながりを示すものはない」と述べた。

容疑者の氏名を公表せず、イスラム過激派組織との関係の有無についても明らかにしなかった。

中東で比較的安定しているヨルダンでは、こうした暴力事件は極めて異例だ。

items.summary: Parliament authorised Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Monday to take "all necessary measures" to help Saudi Arabia defend itself — a move that could push Cairo more directly into the conflict between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.
items.body:
Parliament authorised Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Monday to take "all necessary measures" to help Saudi Arabia defend itself — a move that could push Cairo more directly into the conflict between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.
Sisi had [USN:L6N46403J TEXT:"asked parliament"] to approve military support for Egypt's Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requested help in fighting the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] — southern gateway to the Red Sea and Egypt's Suez Canal.
At least two-thirds of the chamber backed the measure, according to an official parliamentary statement.
Parliament voted in closed session without publishing the tally, and no formal Saudi request for Egyptian troops has been announced.
The statement did not specify what kind of support Egypt would provide. Taher al-Khouly, deputy head of parliament’s legislative committee, told Reuters that Egypt would send forces to Saudi Arabia in coordination between the two countries and at Saudi Arabia’s request.
Several opposition groups opposed or declined to back the move. The Civil Democratic Movement, a coalition of opposition parties, rejected Egyptian military involvement in a regional war and said last week that Cairo’s role should focus on mediation.
The Egyptian Social Democratic Party had said its lawmakers would abstain, citing a lack of information on the mission’s aims, duration and cost, while saying it remained supportive of Saudi Arabia.
Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries, but it has not publicly engaged in direct combat or joined the Mecca [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"mutual defence"] pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"signed in August"].
Ministers from the pact’s member countries held an emergency meeting in Riyadh [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"earlier this month"] and agreed to ensure the “rapid deployment” of forces and military capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan approved the agreement last week, whileTurkey's parliament began ratifying it [USN:L6N4660OA TEXT:"last week"].
Top officials from the three Mecca pact countries were meeting Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday in [USN:L2N46C041 TEXT:"a push to de-escalate the conflict"].
Britain said [USN:SPN46200R TEXT:"last week"] it would deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets on missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks.
SISI SPELLS OUT LIMITS OF EGYPTIAN SUPPORT FOR SAUDIS The Cairo parliament had postponed the vote last week as Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen.
Abdelatty said afterwards that Cairo advocated exploring [USN:L1N4680Z9 TEXT:""every opportunity""] to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically.
Essam Farid, the speaker of the Senate, said Egypt’s position was "purely defensive" and aimed at defending Saudi territory, borders, sovereignty and holy sites against external attack. He said that it would not extend to an attack on Yemen and that Egypt stands with its brothers as "a shield that protects, not a sword that attacks".
Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war, in March 2015.
At that time it acted mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role.
Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the 1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War.
Yahya Ali al-Rai, speaker of Yemen's Houthi-run House of Representatives, last week urged the Cairo parliament to reject the proposal, saying Egypt would be threatening its own national security and internal stability.
The Senate speaker told the chamber he had received a letter from Ahmed Obeid bin Daghr, head of Yemen’s Shura Council, which is aligned with the internationally recognised government, backing Egypt’s participation in defending Saudi Arabia. Bin Daghr said the position reflected the will of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, according to the speaker.
Saudi Arabia is a major political and financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi.
Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran .
The Houthis have attacked [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and the state oil company [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
The Saudi crown prince had sought military help from the US, but President Donald Trump did not agree to strikes on the Houthis, people familiar with the matter told Reuters in September. Washington told Riyadh that it would help with intelligence sharing and targeting, they added.
(This story has been corrected to change the attribution of the remarks to Sisi, not the letter, in paragraph 13.)

items.title: Surgery Partners to be taken private by Bon Secours affiliate in $5.7 billion deal
items.author: Christy Santhosh
items.creator: Christy Santhosh
items.summary: Surgery Partners said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%.
items.body:
Surgery Partners (SGRY.O) said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%.
Private equity group Bain Capital, which has been a minority shareholder since 2017 and owns 39% of Surgery Partners, will back the deal and retain a major ownership stake after closing, the companies said.
The remaining shareholders will receive $23.50 per share, implying a premium of 49% to the stock's last close.
The deal, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, highlights a growing push into outpatient surgery by healthcare operators, with not-for-profit health system Ascension having purchased surgical firm AmSurg for $3.9 billion earlier this year.
The addition of Surgery Partners will expand Bon Secours Mercy Health's US footprint well beyond its more than 45 hospitals, according to the hospital system, adding over 200 sites across 30 states and about 5,000 affiliated physicians.
The deal also ends a two-year strategic review during which Surgery Partners drew interest from potential buyers including Bain Capital, [USN:L4N3SK0YE TEXT:"whose bid to"] take the company private last year was rebuffed.
Surgery Partners operates outpatient surgery centers, short-stay hospitals and related healthcare services across the US.
"From a strategic perspective, there is some market overlap in Ohio and Kentucky, but the potential transaction would substantially broaden the system's (Bon Secours Mercy Health) national footprint, so we do not expect meaningful FTC antitrust risk issues," said Mizuho analyst Ann Hynes.
Hynes said Bain retaining its ownership position under the proposed transaction is expected to help the deal close.
In 2025, Surgery Partners generated $3.31 billion in revenue and reported an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share.

items.title: Netanyahu touts Trump endorsement on eve of vote, suggests they may restart war on Iran
items.author: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
items.creator: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
items.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".
items.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".
"US President Donald Trump has come with a friendship that has never existed before between an Israeli prime minister and an American president. And it is doubtful we will ever have such a friendly president again," Netanyahu said in a televised appearance late on Sunday night. "He has another two years, and he says he is calling on you to vote for me."
In his own social media post on Sunday, Trump, who launched the Iran war jointly with Netanyahu in February, said: "Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!"
Netanyahu said Trump was willing to take action "that would finally, finally, remove the Iranian threat", but only as long as Netanyahu himself remains in power.
"And I have already instructed the Mossad and the IDF (military) to bring down this regime, to bring down this regime because that is the only way to put an end to this threat," Netanyahu said, referring to Israel's main intelligence service and military.
Asked for comment on Netanyahu's remarks, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said: “As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait."
"The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]," Kelly added via email, referring to the November 3 vote in the US.
Trump first endorsed Netanyahu on October 18, reiterating his support in a post on Truth Social on Sunday.
Asked by reporters later on Monday whether Netanyahu had requested the second endorsement, Trump said: "I never spoke about it."
"I put out both endorsements. I put out both... I think he's done a very good job as prime minister under very trying conditions."
Netanyahu's leading opponent, centrist former military Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, posted his own comments on social media, praising Trump as "a true friend of Israel".
"I value his efforts and his commitment to Israel’s security, and I am confident that he will work in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people."
EISENKOT ACCUSES NETANYAHU OF FEAR-MONGERING Tuesday's vote, Israel's first since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, is the first chance for voters to deliver a [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"verdict on the worst security failure"] in generations and the wars on multiple fronts that followed.
With Netanyahu already at the helm of the most right-wing government in Israeli history, politics have shifted even further to the right. Nearly all Jewish-led parties, including that of the hawkish Eisenkot, now [USN:L6N4660BW TEXT:"oppose the "two-state solution" that underpinned decades of peace negotiations"] with the Palestinians.
But many voters say the divisive politics of Israel's longest-serving leader make the country weaker. Polls suggest Netanyahu's Likud Party will lose seats, potentially depriving his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties of its narrow majority.
Eisenkot and an array of opposition parties ranging from the rump of the centre-left to the right, also have no clear path to unseat him.
Netanyahu, 77, is an unrivaled master of political survival: the only time since 2009 that opponents managed to wrest him briefly from the premiership, it took four inconclusive elections within two years to get him out. He was back 18 months later.
Neither side planned major public events for Monday. But both posted on social media, drumming on the election's major themes — for Netanyahu, that he is the only leader with the mettle to face down Israel's enemies; for his opponents, that his divisive politics have weakened the country.
Netanyahu shared an AI-generated video on Monday of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, whose father Ali Khamenei was killed on the first night of US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Lying in a hospital bed, the younger Khamenei says his own vote would be "definitely not Bibi. Another term like this and I will be meeting my father sooner than expected."
On Sunday Netanyahu posted a computer-generated photo of a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv, saying Israel was in existential danger from Iran.
[USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot responded"] by accusing him of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies, and threats—including images of nuclear bombs in the heart of Tel Aviv. This time, it won’t work for him."
Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu carries its own political risks a week before a legislative election in which his own Republicans are seeking to hold onto power.
The Iran war is deeply unpopular in the United States, blamed for a surge in prices especially for fuel. Major fighting has been suspended for months after ceasefire negotiations held without Israeli participation.
items.raw_description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".

items.title: Anthropic's soaring sales, steep losses put AI frenzy to IPO test
items.author: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
items.creator: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
items.summary: Anthropic took a big step closer to a potentially record-breaking IPO on Monday, even as it revealed steep losses and security concerns that could test investors' enthusiasm for the AI heavyweight.
items.body:
Anthropic took a big step closer to a potentially record-breaking IPO on Monday, even as it revealed steep losses and security concerns that could test investors' enthusiasm for the AI heavyweight.
AI has captured investors' imagination with the promise of a technological leap that could transform businesses, accelerate scientific breakthroughs and unlock vast productivity gains.
That has fueled enormous investments in computing infrastructure and AI development, while also stoking skepticism over the scale and pace of the spending.
Anthropic's listing comes at a critical time for global markets as investors closely assess whether the billions of dollars being poured into the technology will generate returns to justify sky-high valuations.
"There is still enormous excitement about AI's potential to transform businesses, turbocharge productivity and reshape entire industries, but investors are becoming more discerning," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
Anthropic's net loss in the first half of 2026 [USN:L4N4661JI TEXT:"widened sharply"] to $80.7 billion, largely due to a non-operating item related to bonds convertible into the company's shares.
Despite the huge expenses, its operating loss for the same period narrowed to $693 million and its adjusted operating income swung to a positive $1.62 billion compared with a loss of $1.85 billion a year ago.
The company, which is expected to go public before Thanksgiving, said its revenue grew a staggering 1,368% in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but it warned in the prospectus that its revenue growth rate could decline and fluctuate from time to time.
The filing [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"confirmed a series of Reuters "][USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"exclusives"] that offered an early peek at its contents before Anthropic made it public, including details of its financial performance, growth trajectory and IPO plans.
Its prospectus details the risks from the powerful technology, from potential misuse and security threats to concerns that advanced systems could produce outputs that "could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative", including behavior resembling blackmail.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei [USN:L1N45403P TEXT:"has called for a slowdown"] in the development of AI.
VALUATION EXPECTATIONS Some current and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"are valuing Anthropic"] at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"recent investor event"].
"The offering is for the faithful, that sooner or later, they're going to get some return on that invested capital," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital.
Anthropic's IPO [USN:L6N46216E TEXT:"currently stands alone"] in what was once expected to be a crowded fall listing market. Analysts [USN:L6N46C0UF TEXT:"said"] that would give it access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions.
"Anthropic's IPO will establish a benchmark for valuing leading AI labs, influencing both upcoming listings and confidence in the companies funding the AI infrastructure build-out," IPOX research associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.
Analysts expect valuations of the AI sector to correct as [USN:L6N4611C1 TEXT:"investor unease"] with the debt-fueled AI investment boom roils equity and debt markets. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have also added to investor caution.
"Anthropic is entering an IPO market that is far more challenging than the summer. Investors were not questioning valuations the same way a few months ago," said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs.
BALANCING AI'S PROMISES AND PERILS Anthropic said more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30% of Global 2000 firms were its customers that generated at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30.
The IPO comes as Anthropic's own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviors including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation.
"Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures," the prospectus said.
The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud services providers such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical infrastructure parts. These relationships can create "dependencies and potential vulnerabilities", it said.
Anthropic, which [USN:L4N41X0QE TEXT:"did not reveal"] the terms of its offering, will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" after the [USN:L4N469189 TEXT:"IPO closes"].
SCORCHING PACE OF GROWTH Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers who left OpenAI after disagreements over governance and AI safety, was [USN:L4N4251UW TEXT:"valued at $965 billion"] in a funding round in May. It remains locked in a fierce battle with OpenAI to lead the race to build the most advanced AI systems.
The company named Netflix's billionaire co-founder Reed Hastings as its lead independent director. In keeping with Nasdaq rules, Anthropic identified itself as a "controlled company" based on the power of its Long-Term Benefit Trust to elect a majority of its board.
The company said it expects compute and infrastructure expenses to rise in absolute dollars and remain its largest operating expense.
Anthropic has committed more than $600 billion to computing deals with partners including Amazon and Google, ranking among the largest AI infrastructure commitments on record.
Anthropic's IPO follows that of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which rewrote the IPO record books in June, when it [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"priced"] a $75 billion offering that valued the company at $1.75 trillion.
Goldman Sachs secured the prestigious lead-left role on Anthropic's IPO, working alongside Morgan Stanley, which is also a lead underwriter. Both banks declined to comment.
Twenty other banks were named as underwriters with Morgan Stanley serving as stabilization agent, overseeing the stock's early trading. The IPO mandates mark another win for the two banks, which also held lead roles in SpaceX's IPO.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 26 : Cadence Design Systems on Monday launched a portfolio of AI models tuned to help design computer chips, deepening its open-source model work with Nvidia and diverging from rival Synopsys' recent deal with OpenAI.
Both companies make software used to design computing chips — a process that involves arranging billions of transistors precisely to meet cost and performance targets — and are racing to have AI "agents" use those tools on behalf of human engineers to speed up the process.
The new suite, called Cadence Maestro, introduced on Monday, was built in part on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron model and secured with Nvidia's OpenShell safety technology, the companies said.
Cadence said customers can run the models on its own cloud or any public cloud, or keep them entirely in-house behind their own firewalls and data centers.

Shares of Cadence, which reports earnings after market close on Monday, rose 3.9 per cent after the announcement.
Customers can also fine-tune the models on their own chip designs, and early results show up to 30 per cent higher quality and up to five times better cost-efficiency than general-purpose models, it added.
The Cadence approach contrasts with that of its largest competitor, Synopsys, which on September 30 said it would develop an AI model with OpenAI and share revenue with the ChatGPT maker. That model, GPT-Synopsys, will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure.
Paul Cunningham, a Cadence senior vice president, framed Maestro as model-agnostic, saying, "there are more (AI) model providers out there than there are (chip design software) vendors."
When asked whether Cadence might strike its own deals with proprietary AI labs, Cunningham said both open- and closed-weight approaches were being "pursued equally," and that working with commercial labs was "part of the Maestro vision," though he declined to elaborate.
The first Maestro models will reach select early-access customers in the fourth quarter, Cadence said.

Oct 26 : T-Mobile on Monday unveiled wireless plans that let customers pick and swap perks from Netflix to DoorDash, moving away from its traditional strategy of locking benefits into fixed plan tiers. 
The move mirrors customizable offerings from rivals such as Verizon, but T-Mobile's new plans include selected streaming, music and other subscriptions at no extra cost beyond the monthly plan price. 
• T-Mobile is betting that offering greater control over benefits will attract customers spending on multiple subscriptions, as competition among US carriers moves beyond network coverage and smartphone promotions
• Netflix was the most popular benefit in a pilot launched in early October, T-Mobile Chief Marketing Officer Allan Samson told Reuters in an interview

BRUSSELS, Oct 26 : The European Commission said on Monday it had accepted Chinese online retail platform Temu's action plan to remedy a breach of the EU's Digital Services Act, following a fine imposed on the company in May.
The plan focuses on five measures to remedy the breach, and Temu now has four months to conduct an interim risk assessment, the Commission, which acts as EU regulator, said in a statement.
The Commission had imposed a €200 million ($224.08 million) fine on Temu in May for not doing enough to stop the sale of illegal products.
A spokesperson for Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, said it welcomed the Commission's approval of its plan under which the company will have to assess possible shortcomings of its content moderation system, among other steps.
Temu, along with Shein and other ecommerce platforms, has been hit by the EU imposing €3 fees on low-value ecommerce packages since the start of July. Parcels worth less than €150 previously entered the bloc duty-free.
($1 = 0.8925 euros)

items.title: Brazil's Lula hangs on, but his final term promises to be toughest yet
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle
items.summary: Congress has amassed significant power over government spending in the past decade, which could frustrate Lula's promises to maintain his signature welfare programs.
items.body:
Brazil's octogenarian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva faces an uphill battle from day one of his final term, analysts say, with his plans hemmed in by economic headwinds and a right-wing Congress.
Already the country's oldest president, Lula overcame a first-round loss to pull off a [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"surprise runoff victory"] against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday, securing 51.8% of votes and a record fourth term just two days before his 81st birthday.
He will take office on January 5 after winning what he has said was his last election, hanging on to power in a country that has swung dramatically to the right since his first electoral victory in 2002.
FISCAL POLICY 'HIS BIGGEST CHALLENGE' "Lula has shown that he still is the dominant political figure of his era, but he is weaker," Michael Ahn Paarlberg of the Center for International Policy think tank said.
Brazil's incoming Congress is its [USN:L1N45L166 TEXT:"most conservative"] since the country's return to democracy in the 1980s, with Bolsonaro's party and its allies enjoying majorities in both chambers.
"He's likely to be a lame duck from the start," said Oliver Stuenkel, an international relations professor at Sao Paulo's Getulio Vargas Foundation, who predicted Lula would struggle to build a coalition to pass much of his agenda.
As of Monday morning, Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, had yet to concede, and Lula faced the prospect of adversaries in Congress who do not recognize his win, analysts said.
In addition, Congress has amassed significant power over government spending in the past decade, which could frustrate Lula's promises to maintain his signature welfare programs.
Meanwhile, his government forecasts meager 2.3% economic growth next year, adding to fiscal challenges worsened by high interest rates and public debt that has grown past 82% of GDP, the highest since the pandemic.
"On the broad macroeconomic outlook, things are not looking great," Monica de Bolle, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, said.
A hostile Congress "will make it very hard to push any reform through Congress and even try to manage the budget," she said.
Lula's promises to ensure minimum wage increases remain above inflation are among those that clash with growing pressure to get debt under control. Lula’s aides have also signaled he will keep pushing to curtail tax breaks, but lawmakers have repeatedly resisted measures that raise the effective tax burden.
"Fiscal policy remains Lula's biggest economic challenge," said Andres Abadia, chief Latin American economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, as growing mandatory spending and high interest costs leave little room to cut deficits.
Analysts said an economic crisis could even spur Lula's impeachment, with some drawing comparisons to Brazil's 2014-2016 crisis, which preceded the impeachment of Lula's ally Dilma Rousseff.
"I think the campaign for Lula's impeachment begins now," said Paulo Kramer, a political scientist who worked on former President Bolsonaro's first campaign and has spoken to people close to his son.
Investors [USN:L2N46C051 TEXT:"reacted nervously"] on Monday morning, sending Brazilian assets sharply lower as markets reassessed the country's fiscal outlook under Lula.
SENATE STUMBLING BLOCK Congress is likely to block or slow Lula's [USN:L1N45K0U9 TEXT:"appointments to key roles"] in institutions such as the Supreme Court and the central bank, analysts say.
For the first time since Brazil returned to democracy, the executive branch will be clearly at odds with the Senate, Lucas de Aragao, a partner at Brasilia-based consultancy Arko Advice, said.
"Lula will have some room to negotiate in the lower house by giving centrist parties more space, but in the Senate he will have to bargain issue by issue and adjust his legislative agenda to fit what the opposition wants," Aragao added.
Bolsonaro's allies in the incoming Senate have also [USN:L6N45U19L TEXT:"vowed to impeach"] Justice Alexandre de Moraes, escalating their long-running fight with a powerful judiciary that has often aligned with Lula, blocking key right-wing legislation and shaping policy on everything from Indigenous rights to the internet.

Netflix is not growing as expected. Users don’t open the app

Netflix's shares have slipped by about 29 per cent, affecting the company’s overall growth. Its advertising will also face a slump of about $300 million compared to its earlier projections.

Sagrika Kissu

26 October, 2026 05:38 pm IST

Facebook

Representational image | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

New Delhi: Netflix is losing out on its viewers. A Bloomberg report has noted that the once loyal army of Netflix users are not watching the streaming service as much as they did earlier. 

“Customers aren’t opening the app on as many days a month as they did a couple of years ago, said the people who asked not to be identified because the data is confidential,” the Bloomberg report read.

The report added that the customers are also spending less time watching Netflix. While the total time on the app has increased, sources told Bloomberg that it’s because more customers were added. But individually, the users are watching less.

Show Full Article

“Netflix has increased its programming budget and is expanding into new categories, such as podcasts and live sports, to attract new customers and retain old ones,” said the report.

As per a firm named Apptopia, a firm that tracks mobile app use , the share of US subscribers who didn’t open the app rose by 16.6 per cent in the third quarter, compared to last year. 

Netflix has not produced many hit TV shows and films this year. But its executives have identified several reasons behind this decline: new user interface to greater competition, worse programming to dearth of marketing outside the service. 

And now, Netflix is worried. In 2022, the company started cracking down on password sharing. But the reason is not password sharing but users finding less value in the content on the platform.

“At first, executives assumed it would be short-term, because fewer people were using each account. But the trend has continued, raising the risk that people are using each account. But the trend has continued, raising the risk that people are finding less value in the service or spending more time with rivals,” the report said .

Also read: Does air pollution cause dementia? What new studies say on what it does to the brain

 

Not growing as fast as expected
The decline in usage has been modest at 2 per cent. The shares have slipped by about 29 per cent, affecting the company’s overall growth. Netflix said its advertising will also face a slump of about $300 million dollars compared to its earlier projections. 

Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos said that viewership in the US is not particularly “growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like.” But he added that the company is doing well outside the US.

Netflix was founded in August 1997 by Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph to make movie rentals more accessible. Back then, it brought a major shift in the movie rental industry as people didn’t have to visit physical stores but could order DVDs online and get them delivered to their homes.

It was in 2007 when Netflix launched its streaming service “Watch Now.” It had a library of around a thousand movies and TV shows that users could watch online instantly.

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

Oct 26 : SpaceX said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.
Each lease will run a little over five years from the day the equipment arrives, according to a regulatory filing.
The deal highlights SpaceX's heavy spending, as it tries to capitalize on surging demand for computing power to help bankroll its Moon and Mars ambitions.
The company aims to finalize the deal by the end of the year. The leases are expected to start in the first half of 2027, once the chips are delivered.

Oct 26 : Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation.
CoreWeave, which has become a poster child for mounting concerns over heavy AI spending, declined 1.6 per cent, while Nebius Group fell 4 per cent and IREN lost 1.5 per cent.
Shares of Applied Digital shed 2 per cent.
In a social media post on Sunday, Musk said that neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, adding that SpaceX would not buy any neocloud companies, calling it "pointless".

"200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he said.
"Musk is correct. You're going to need another source of revenue and profits in order to finance these projects moving forward. The cost of capital is too high to make the returns attractive," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital in New York.
In an email to Reuters, a CoreWeave spokesperson said that the company continues to see opportunities to finance its growth, underscored by qualities such as "differentiated technology".
Musk was not alone in flagging the risks to the sector.
Earlier this month, research firm Gartner said CoreWeave was at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds most exposed to the increasing leverage, and added that 80 per cent of the companies could cease independent operations by 2032.
Some brokerages expect AI spending to shoot past a trillion dollars next year, adding to investor concerns about the repercussions of severe dependence on debt, at a time when AI assets face rapid depreciation and markets price in more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
Bonds of Nebius maturing in 2034 and those of CoreWeave expiring in 2033 have hit record lows on the concerns.
CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and TeraWulf have reported quarterly losses over the past one year, while IREN has not turned a profit in the past three quarters, raising scrutiny over profitability.
Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen more than 30 per cent this month alone. Investors betting on their fall have raked in at least $6 billion in paper profits.

Macron keeps lid on violence but public anger in France shows few signs of abating

The standoff leaves the govt in a quandary, with calls growing for more spending on services when it’s under pressure from a fast-growing debt burden & surging borrowing costs.

Alan Katz

26 October, 2026 05:25 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

A fire breaks out at a demonstration in Paris, France, on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

French President Emmanuel Macron bet that a massive police presence could avoid a repeat of the violence that stunned the country on Oct. 17. He won that wager, but isn’t any closer to resolving underlying anger that’s fueled mass protests in France and shows few signs of abating.

Hundreds of thousands took part in the demonstrations across consecutive weekends, with turnout remaining high despite worries about further violence, Macron’s warning against action unless organized by labor unions, and poor weather.

The standoff leaves the government in a quandary, with calls growing for more spending on services when it’s under pressure from a fast-growing debt burden and surging borrowing costs, and with presidential elections on the horizon.

Show Full Article

Student groups are continuing their call for further protests over what they say is the absence of concrete measures to address concerns about school conditions, needed funding, and the system for distributing university slots. Unions have called for a major day of strikes and protests on Nov. 5.

“We’re not giving up on anything,” Manon Moret, secretary general of student union UNEF, told reporters during the protest in Paris. “On the demands of young people, the €10 billion, and the issue of selectivity” in university placements.

But France doesn’t have the budget leeway to mount a dramatic financial response. While it dodged a downgrade by Moody’s Ratings on Friday, it’s struggling to reduce its yawning budget deficit ahead of the April election, and has seen borrowing costs jump as investors demand higher premiums to buy its debt.

A closely watched gauge of bond risk rose last week to levels last seen during the euro-area debt crisis. The spread between 10-year yields in France and Germany, the region’s safe asset, reached 178 basis points on Thursday, against 85 basis points at the start of September.

Protest Numbers
There’s been no let-up on the demonstrators’ side so far. Some 410,000 people took part in the weekend marches across the country, according to the Interior Ministry, compared with its estimate of 550,000 for Oct. 17. The left-wing CGT union put its estimate much higher, at about 800,000 for each day.

On Monday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said he expected protests to continue. “From here till the elections, and in the very short term, the situation is extremely tense,” Nunez said on BFM TV, noting that some demonstrations have already been called for Oct. 31.

“Halloween evening is typically lively,” he said. “Of course we’ll deploy a very robust plan.”

The government has indicated it may shift its position, at least slightly, this week. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is scheduled to meet with student representatives on Monday after they’d been requesting a meeting for weeks. On Saturday, Finance Minister Roland Lescure floated the idea of advancing by a couple of months the annual increase in France’s minimum wage, which is indexed to inflation.

“Yes, we’re constrained financially,” Lescure said in an interview on Franceinfo radio. “But we’ve been creative.” He noted that the government had released strategic stocks of diesel and issued subsidies for high-mileage drivers to ease the pressure of high energy costs.

Read more: France Avoids Moody’s Downgrade in Reprieve After Week of Crisis

Macron’s government can at least consider how to convince protesters to stay home after the past weekend’s marches went ahead with far less violence than the week before, when authorities were caught flat-footed and demonstrations descended into chaos.

Rioters a week earlier attacked public buildings and broke into stores across the country, including in the capital, fought with police, and set fire to cars. Macron, the target of much of the anger, on Thursday acknowledged “planning failings and elements of surprise.”

As a result, the government deployed some 70,000 security officials on Saturday, including elite anti-terror forces. It also banned marches in several cities and forced demonstrators in Paris to take a route that confined them to the eastern edge of the city. A total of 1,435 people were arrested on Saturday, Nuñez said.

Next Saturday may be another test. At least one protest website has already called for another round of demonstrations on Oct. 31, while Union Syndicale Solidaires co-head Murielle Guilbert said she expected unions to call for new protests as well.

During the largely left-wing protests across France on Saturday, groups regularly shouted “Macron, resign!” The slogan also proved popular at the far-right National Rally’s congress in Orleans over the weekend. “Don’t worry,” party president Jordan Bardella said during a speech on Sunday. “He’ll be gone before long.”

Macron’s term ends in May, and term limits prevent him from running again in 2027.

A survey published in Le Parisien newspaper on Saturday showed that the National Rally’s candidate, Marine Le Pen, is firmly in the lead for that election, with far-left France Unbowed leader, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, in second place, ahead of various centrist contenders.

Speaking on Sunday, Le Pen basked in that advantage. “Everyone in France agrees with us; the battle is won over the assessment” of how France is doing, she said. “Our goal is to offer a real alternative, which is not a revolutionary act, but a natural cycle in democracy.”

Wider Protests
Protests continued elsewhere in Europe during the weekend, too, over a range of issues including the cost of living, housing and education. About 100 people were arrested in central Barcelona, where protesters burned containers, vandalized shops, and threw stones at police.

Thousands marched in cities across Italy amid a heavy police presence, with scattered clashes reported. Albania’s capital of Tirana continued to be rocked by demonstrations against its prime minister. Tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets were used by police as protestors threw stones and set fires.

items.author: Ng Hong Siang
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has been a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.

CNA Explains: Why are the Houthis targeting Saudi airports?

Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has been a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.

Smoke and flames rise from King Khalid Airport after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked the airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Oct 8, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a social media video. (Image: Social Media via Reuters)

FAST

Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has become a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels, disrupting flights and raising concerns about the security of civilian aviation in the kingdom.
On Monday (Oct 26), the Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh, after the Iran-backed group claimed another attack on King Khalid International Airport.
The latest incident came as flights resumed at the airport following weeks of disruption, with the Houthis warning airlines and travellers that the facility remained "unsafe" and a "military target".
But the Houthis' attacks on Saudi airports are not new. As far back as November 2017, the group fired a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport, which Saudi authorities said they intercepted.
